title: Reserve Bank Amendment (Australian Reconstruction and Development Board) Bill 2013
short_title: Reserve Bank Amendment (Australian Reconstruction and Development Board) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish an Australian Reconstruction and Development Board within the Reserve Bank to develop rural financial policy and restructure financial arrangements threatening agricultural viability.
The new board would research risks, offer tailored finance and use the bank’s capital for reconstruction and development, including work involving associated industries and infrastructure.
The substantive amendments would start on the 28th day after Royal Assent, and the Reserve Bank Board’s policy would prevail where the boards’ policies conflicted.
changes: The bank would gain an express power to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
The new board would include the Governor, a bank representative and seven members with relevant rural or agricultural experience.
Parliamentary chambers and committees could request consideration of matters or reports within the board’s functions.
summary.affected: Agricultural enterprises, associated industries and infrastructure, other sectors identified as at risk, and the Reserve Bank’s boards are affected.
